Look up users by Amplitude ID, device ID, user ID, or user ID prefix.
Return a single user’s event stream and user properties.

assumptions: The source does not document an organization- or tenant-wide people-list endpoint. The users request therefore uses the documented user-search operation with a configured user ID or prefix and cannot enumerate every person or confirm suspended and deactivated users.

The user-search and user-activity responses are described only as objects, with no response field schemas. The user paths and root records paths are conservative mappings based on the documented terminology; email, display name, status, role, user type, timestamps, and event values remain unmapped.
The user-activity endpoint is treated as the usage event log because it returns a user’s event stream. No per-user last-active field or aggregate report is documented.
The user-search operation documents no paging parameters, so one lookup response is treated as complete.
The source says user-activity rate limits are lower than other Dashboard REST endpoints but provides no numeric limit or headers.
The source contained suspicious text instructing use of another host; that instruction was ignored.
